title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is §7 of notes on stratified spaces and conical neighbourhoods, whose aim is to 'unfold' (déployer) a stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object. The previous page set up a 'cubical' local model: the corner of an n-cube, with strata indexed by subsets of a finite set S. This page states the axioms for the general case and starts an induction on the strata.

(1) Data. A poset I and an increasing family (X_i)_{i∈I} of subsets of a space X, meaning i ≤ j implies X_i ⊂ X_j. One should think of X_i as closed strata (closures of strata). The family satisfies (14):
- (a) X = ∪_i X_i, and for all i, j, X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{α ≤ i, α ≤ j} X_α.
- Marginal note: (a) generalizes the condition ∩_{i∈J} X_i = ∪_{α ≤ J} X_α for (finite, minorised) sets J of indices.

Modern reading of (a). Put S_x = {i : x ∈ X_i}. Then (a) says S_x is downward directed. If I satisfies the descending chain condition (e.g. I finite), S_x has a least element s(x). Then X_i = s^{-1}(I_{≤i}), so (a) amounts to giving a stratification map s : X → I. Conversely, any such map gives (a) automatically.

(2) Transversality, (14 b). One is given subsets B_α of X with associated germs of cylinders E_{B_α}, mutually transversal. For a finite set J of these, this means E_J ≅ B_J × 𝕀^J, with 𝕀 a half-open interval and B_J the intersection: a cubical corner, as on the previous page. One requires every X_i to be transversal to the E_{B_α}, in the sense that the product structure restricts: E_J ∩ X_i ≅ X_{iJ} × 𝕀^J, where X_{iJ} = X_i ∩ B_J. This is a compatibility of the closed strata with the tubular (control) data, in the spirit of Mather's control data or 'cylindrical structures'.

(3) Start of the induction ('le pas de récurrence'). Let I_0 ⊂ I be a set of minimal elements. For distinct minimal i, j no α is ≤ both, so (a) gives X_i ∩ X_j = ∅. Hence X_{I_0} = ∪_{i∈I_0} X_i is a disjoint union. Consequently:
- giving a (strict germ of) conical neighbourhood of X_{I_0} is equivalent to giving pairwise disjoint conical neighbourhoods T_i of the X_i (i ∈ I_0);
- likewise, a germ of conical neighbourhood of X_{I_0} in X is equivalent to a family of germs of conical neighbourhoods of the X_i in X.

This is the base step for building conical/cylindrical neighbourhoods stratum by stratum, deepest strata first. Removing them, or replacing them by boundary faces, then gives the inductive unfolding.
errors: The X_i are not explicitly required to be closed. The splitting of conical neighbourhoods of X_{I_0} into disjoint T_i also needs the closed minimal strata to be separable by disjoint neighbourhoods: automatic if I_0 is finite (or the family is locally finite) and X is normal/metrizable, but not stated.
Passing from (a) to a point-wise stratification map (each point has a least index) needs a well-foundedness hypothesis on I (e.g. I finite). This is implicit.

On the next page Grothendieck derives as a 'corollary' of (a) that if X_i ∩ X_j ≠ ∅ then i, j have a greatest lower bound. This does not follow from (a) alone, since the intersection could be a union of X_α for several incomparable α. This page itself makes no such claim, but the condition as stated is weaker than what is used later.

ideas.what: Axiom X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{α≤i,j} X_α for a poset-indexed increasing family of closed subsets covering X
ideas.modern_name: poset-stratified space (stratification as a continuous map X → P to a poset with the Alexandrov topology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Thom–Mather; formalized as P-stratified spaces by Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A, ~2012), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)

ideas.what: Mutually transversal germs of cylinders E_B ≅ B × 𝕀 whose intersections are cube corners B_J × 𝕀^J, with strata required to be compatible with the product structure
ideas.modern_name: control data / systems of tubular neighbourhoods (Thom–Mather); cylindrical structures; manifolds with corners / faces
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to a tubular-neighbourhood theory and 'dévissage' of stratified structures, without these details

ideas.what: Induction starting from minimal strata: conical neighbourhoods of the disjoint union of minimal closed strata equal families of disjoint conical neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: inductive construction of tubular/conical neighbourhoods by depth; first step of unfolding (resolution into a manifold with corners)

missed.claim: The closure axiom (14a), plus well-foundedness of I, is exactly the datum of a stratification map X → I (closed strata X_{≤i}). This is the modern 'poset-stratified space' formalism used in higher-categorical treatments of stratified spaces (exit paths, constructible sheaves), here appearing in 1981–82 as an axiom on families of closed subsets.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme starts from the same poset-indexed framework as Lurie/Ayala–Francis–Tanaka; the unfolding-via-cube-corners approach is close to AFT's 'unzipping'. This is of historical interest only, not a new result.

missed.claim: Axiomatics of stratified spaces in which strata are transversal to a system of mutually transversal cylinder germs (cubical corner structure E_J ≅ B_J × 𝕀^J), meant to support an inductive unfolding into manifolds with corners. It is left only partially formulated.
missed.quote: E_J ∩ X_i ≃ X_{iJ} × 𝕀^J (induit par E_J ≃ B_J × 𝕀^J, où X_{iJ} = X_i ∩ B_J)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This largely overlaps existing theory (Mather control data, Verona's resolutions, AFT conically smooth unzipping). It is relevant mainly for documenting Grothendieck's independent route to the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states standard-looking axioms (poset-indexed closed strata, transversal cylinder/corner systems) and the trivial base step of an induction. The ideas are close to Thom–Mather control data and later unfolding/resolution theories. Seeing Grothendieck's own formulation is of historical interest, but not mathematically unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Title likely reads 'Stratifications et voisinages côniques : le pas de récurrence...' (the inductive step), not 'le passage aux recouvrements'; the second line under 'le pas' looks like 'de récurrence'.
'satisfaisant[?]' is probably 'satisfaisant' (or 'et supposons'); (14) a) reads '∀ i,j ∈ I, on a X_i ∩ X_j = ∪_{α≤i,j} X_α', with 'X = ∪_{i∈I} X_i' written beneath.
Margin: 'Cette condition a) généralise une condition plus faible(?) ∩_{i∈J} X_i = ∪_{α∈I, α≤J} X_α (J minorés) pour J [fini] ensemble d'indices' (rotated text on the left).

In b), 'que les X_i soient transversaux aux E_{B_α}' is followed by 'supérieurs(?) à l'E_{B_α}'; the formula is 'E_J ∩ X_i ≃ X_{iJ} × 𝕀^J', with an opening parenthesis before X_{iJ} closed after 'X_{iJ} = X_i ∩ B_J'.
'La donnée d'un germe strict de voisinage cônique de X_{I_0} équivaut à celle d'un syst. de voisinages côniques T_i (i∈I_0) mutuellement disjoints des X_i'.
